forms: name the point opposite another
say which side east or west is when facing north
say where the sun rises and sets
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G4.NATURA.COMPASS_DIRECTION.CD_POIN.mastery: The child names north, east, south and west in order round a compass, knows north is opposite south and east is opposite west, knows that facing north east is on the right hand and west on the left, and knows the sun rises in the east and sets in the west. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say which direction one place lies from another
turn a direction round (A is north of B, so B is south of A)
say the direction after a turn
read a small table of places
SOCI.G4.NATURA.COMPASS_DIRECTION.CD_DIRE.mastery: Given a map described in words or a small table, the child says the direction from one place to another, reverses it correctly and gives the direction a walker faces after a quarter turn. Map questions are in words or a small described table, and any county named on a map is an imaginary one. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the unit that is part of a county
put county, sub-county and ward in order of size
say whether a place is inside or outside the county
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..mastery: The child knows a county is divided into sub-counties and a sub-county into wards, that a sub-county is smaller than its county, and that a neighbouring county is a different county and not one of its sub-counties. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say which direction a neighbour lies from the county
name the neighbour in a given direction
say which counties share a boundary
read a small table of neighbours
SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..mastery: Given a described map or table, the child says which neighbouring county lies in each direction, turns the direction round, and names only the counties that share a boundary, not those further away. Map questions are in words or a small described table, and any county named on a map is an imaginary one. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say which county is larger from the areas given
say about how many times larger one is
tell size from population
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G4.NATURA.LOCATION_AND_SIZE_OF_THE..mastery: Given the areas of counties in square kilometres, the child says which is larger and about how many times, compares the whole numbers by their size and not by their first digit, and does not mix up the size of a county with the number of people in it. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: name the kind of feature from a description
pick the odd one out
tell a hill from a mountain, a river from a lake, a plain from a valley
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G4.NATURA.PHYSICAL_FEATURES_IN_THE..mastery: The child names a hill (low rounded high ground), a mountain (much higher), a valley (low land between hills or mountains), a plain (wide flat land), a river (water flowing in a channel), a lake (water with land around it) and the ocean coast from a short description. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: match a feature to its use
say why a feature matters to the people near it
pick the false use
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G4.NATURA.PHYSICAL_FEATURES_IN_THE..mastery: The child matches rivers and lakes to water, fish and irrigation, mountains and hills to rain, forests and tourism, plains to farming and building, and the coast to fishing and ports, and does not call a feature useless or give it a use it does not have. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: name the season from its weather
pick the season that has long or short rains
say whether a statement is about one day or a whole season
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.mastery: The child names the four seasons as hot, cold, dry and rainy, matches each to its weather, knows the long rains come around March to May and the short rains around October to December, and does not use the names spring, summer, autumn and winter or call one rainy day a season. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the activity that suits a season
say what a farmer does in a season
say what people wear or sell in a season
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.mastery: The child says farmers plant when the rains begin and harvest and dry crops in the dry season, that people wear warm clothes in the cold season and drink and sell cold drinks in the hot season, and that the seasons do change what people do. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say what rain does to a road
choose the safe thing to do near a flooded road
say what a driver should do in heavy rain
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G4.NATURA.SEASONS_IN_THE_COUNTY.SE_.mastery: The child says rain makes roads slippery, muddy and sometimes flooded and makes it harder to see, that a driver must slow down, and that a person must never cross flooded water, never run across a road, and wait in a safe place. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: name the kind of place from its job
pick the place that is a historic built environment
pick the odd one out
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G4.NATURA.HISTORIC_BUILT_ENVIRONME..mastery: The child says a museum keeps and shows old objects and records, a monument is a structure built to remember a person or event, and a cultural centre shows the way of life of communities, and knows a place is historic because of its age and meaning, not because it is new or big. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the reason a place is kept
say what people gain from visiting
say how to treat a historic place
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G4.NATURA.HISTORIC_BUILT_ENVIRONME..mastery: The child says historic places teach history, keep a community's identity, bring visitors and need to be cared for, and does not say they should be pulled down because they are old. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say who a person depends on for a need
say what a worker gives others
match a place or worker to what it gives
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.INTERDEPENDENCE_OF_PEOPL..mastery: The child names trade (a farmer sells to a shopkeeper), farming (farmers feed others), the hospital (health workers care for the sick) and places of worship (leaders guide people) as ways people depend on each other, and says that each side needs the other. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the benefit of sharing work
say what happens when nobody depends on anyone
say who gains from a trade
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.INTERDEPENDENCE_OF_PEOPL..mastery: The child says depending on each other gives us goods and services we cannot make ourselves, brings income, lets people use different skills and builds friendship, and does not say a family can supply every need alone. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say whether an area is dense or sparse from the figures
pick the reason an area has many or few people
tell distribution from total population
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G4.PEOPLE.POPULATION_DISTRIBUTION.P.mastery: The child says population distribution is how people are spread over an area, that dense means many people for the space and sparse few, and gives reasons: many people live where soil is fertile, rain is reliable, there is water, work, roads, health care and security, and few where it is very dry, steep, flooded or unsafe. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: name the aspect an item belongs to
match a practice to its aspect
say whether a statement about culture is true
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G4.SOCIAL.ASPECTS_OF_TRADITIONAL_C..mastery: The child names the six aspects of traditional culture (dressing, food, housing, artefacts, sports and games, festivals and ceremonies), sorts everyday examples into them, knows culture is alive and not only the past, and knows communities in one county can have different traditions. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: name the value a learner shows
pick the action that shows a value
say why a value matters
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G4.SOCIAL.THE_SCHOOL.SC_VALUES.mastery: Given a short school situation, the child names the value it shows (respect, honesty, responsibility, hard work, unity, cleanliness) and says why it matters, and does not treat values as the same thing as written rules or punishments. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say whether a resource is natural or made by people
match a resource to the activity that uses it
say whether an activity is economic
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ECONOMIC_ACTIVITIES_IN_T..mastery: The child names natural resources (soil, water, forests, minerals, wildlife, climate), matches them to the activities that use them (farming, fishing, mining, lumbering, tourism, trading, manufacturing) and knows an economic activity earns a living or a product, which play and rest do not. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick a reason an activity matters
say what an activity gives a family
say what an activity gives the county
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ECONOMIC_ACTIVITIES_IN_T..mastery: The child says economic activities give food, income, jobs, raw materials for industries and money for the county, and does not say they only help the rich or only give money. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: name the raw material or the product
say what an industry does to a raw material
say whether a place is an industry
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.INDUSTRIES_IN_THE_COUNTY..mastery: The child says an industry makes or processes goods from raw materials (milk to packed milk, sugarcane to sugar, tea leaves to tea, maize to flour), keeps raw material and product the right way round, and does not call a shop or a farm an industry. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick a benefit of an industry
say who gains from a factory
say what happens to farmers near a factory
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.INDUSTRIES_IN_THE_COUNTY..mastery: The child says industries give jobs, income, a market for farmers, goods to buy and money for the county, and says the benefits reach workers, farmers and shoppers, not only the owner. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the best place for an industry
read where an industry is from a small table
say why an industry is near its raw material or market
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.INDUSTRIES_IN_THE_COUNTY..mastery: Given a described map or table, the child places an industry near its raw material, workers, roads and water and reads where an industry is from the table. Map questions are in words or a small described table, and any county named on a map is an imaginary one. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the project that suits the school's resources
say what a project needs before it starts
say what a project earns or gives
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ENTERPRISE_PROJECT_AT_SC..mastery: The child names school projects (kitchen garden, poultry, tree nursery, bee-keeping, making liquid soap, recycling), chooses the one that suits the land, water and people the school has, and knows a project needs a plan. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the honest action with project money
say how the team should work
say what to do with a mistake or a loss
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G4.RESOUR.ENTERPRISE_PROJECT_AT_SC..mastery: The child says project money is kept honestly and recorded, the team shares the work and decisions, mistakes are reported, and profit belongs to the project and school, not to one person. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: name the quality in a situation
pick the action of a good citizen
say whether a statement about good citizens is true
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.GOOD_CITIZENSHIP_IN_SCHO..mastery: The child names the qualities of a good school citizen (respect, honesty, responsibility, obedience to fair rules, helping others, keeping the school clean, being on time, caring for property) and does not say that only the top learners or those who never speak are good citizens. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick what promotes peace
pick what breaks peace
say what peace means
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.PEACE.PE_FACTORS.mastery: The child says respect, sharing, honesty, listening, fairness, forgiveness and accepting differences promote peace, and that peace means disagreements are settled without hurting anyone, not that nobody ever disagrees. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the peaceful way to react
put the steps of settling a quarrel in order
say who can help
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.PEACE.PE_STRATEGIES.mastery: The child chooses to stay calm, listen, talk it through, say sorry and forgive, and to ask a teacher or peer mediator for help, and does not choose to fight back, take revenge or gossip. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the example that is child abuse
pick the example that is not child abuse
say whether a chore is child labour
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_FORMS.mastery: The child names early and forced marriage, female genital mutilation, slavery, child trafficking, child and forced labour, sexual abuse, abuse of children with special needs and unsafe unauthorised school transport as child abuse, knows that beating and neglect also harm, and knows that light chores at home are not child labour. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick a cause of child abuse
say who is responsible
say whether a custom is a good reason
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_CAUSES.mastery: The child gives causes such as poverty, ignorance, harmful customs, greed, war and the harmful use of alcohol and drugs by adults, and says abuse is never the child's fault and a custom does not make it right. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick an effect of child abuse
say what a child should do who is being hurt
say what a child should do when a friend is hurt
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILD_RIGHTS.CR_EFFECTS.mastery: The child names effects (injury, fear, sadness, dropping out of school, poor health), says a child who is hurt or whose friend is hurt must tell a trusted adult such as a teacher, parent or the Childline helpline on 116, and says harm is not kept secret. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the democratic way to choose
put the steps of a school election in order
say whether a way of choosing is democratic
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.DEMOCRACY_IN_SCHOOL.DS_PR.mastery: The child says democratic processes in school include electing prefects by a secret vote, class meetings, debates and suggestion boxes, puts the election steps in order (nomination, campaign, voting, counting, announcing) and knows a teacher appointing someone is not an election. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick a benefit of democracy
say what the majority and the minority each get
say why everyone should vote
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.DEMOCRACY_IN_SCHOOL.DS_BE.mastery: The child says democracy gives everyone a voice, is fair, builds peace, and makes decisions that most learners accept, and that the choice of the majority is followed while the views of the others are still respected. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick who belongs to the Children's Government
say how members are chosen
say who guides the learners
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILDREN_S_GOVERNMENT_IN..mastery: The child says the Children's Government is made up of learners elected by their classmates, with a leader and ministers or prefects for different areas, guided by a patron teacher, and not by teachers alone. Posts and names vary by school. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick a duty of the Children's Government
pick what it does not do
say who a learner takes a worry to
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.CHILDREN_S_GOVERNMENT_IN..mastery: The child says the Children's Government speaks for learners, helps keep order and cleanliness, organises school activities and passes learners' worries to the teachers, and does not punish learners or run the school in place of the head teacher. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: name the leader from a duty
say what a leader does
pick the odd one out
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.COMMUNITY_LEADERSHIP.CL_L.mastery: The child names religious leaders (guide people in faith and counsel), clan leaders and village elders (settle disputes and guard customs) and the chief (keeps law and order and links the village to the government), and does not say that leaders are only politicians. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the quality of a good leader
say how a good leader acts in a situation
say why leaders must be honest
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.COMMUNITY_LEADERSHIP.CL_Q.mastery: The child says a good leader is honest, fair, listens, serves everyone and sets an example, and does not say a leader is good because he or she is the strongest, the richest or the loudest. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick who is in the county executive
pick who is in the county assembly
tell county government from national government
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.THE_COUNTY_GOVERNMENTS_I..mastery: The child says a county government has a county executive (the Governor, the Deputy Governor and the county executive committee members) and a county assembly (the Members of the County Assembly and the Speaker), and does not mix it up with the President and Members of Parliament. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick a duty of the Governor
pick what the Governor does not do
say who elects the Governor
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.THE_COUNTY_GOVERNMENTS_I..mastery: The child says the Governor is elected by the people of the county for five years, heads the county executive, sees that county laws are carried out, appoints the county executive committee with the assembly's approval and reports on the county, and does not make laws or head the country. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick a duty of the MCA
say whom an MCA represents
pick what an MCA does not do
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G4.CITIZE.THE_COUNTY_GOVERNMENTS_I..mastery: The child says a Member of the County Assembly (MCA) is elected by a ward, makes county laws, approves the county budget, checks the work of the executive and speaks for the people of the ward, and does not carry out the laws or speak for the whole country. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.
